pairs.subject: lazy-section-addressability
pairs.evidence: app/features/insights/analytics/sections/analyticsSections.ts:7 The analytics surface is a ?sec= view switcher that renders only the active section (AnalyticsTab.tsx renders one section per value), not a long page with named scroll locations. A search of the sections directory for scrollIntoView, IntersectionObserver, location.hash, scroll-mt, scrollTo and useInView found nothing, and the only ids elsewhere in analytics/ are form and aria-labelledby ids. So there is no scroll address space here for this subject to govern.

techniques.evidence: app/features/insights/analytics/sections/sectionChunks.tsx:23 The code-split panel gaps reserve height but no outside link or in-page link targets them, so there is nothing for an anchor wrapper to carry.

app/features/insights/analytics/sections/analyticsSections.ts:14 The ids are values for a view-selection query param (picking which view renders), not scroll anchors inside one page. An unknown value falls back to the default view.

app/features/insights/analytics/sections/AnalyticsSectionNav.tsx:28 Navigation swaps app state to a different section. It does not scroll to a lazily mounted target, so there is no hydrate-then-retry protocol to judge.

app/features/insights/analytics/sections/analyticsSections.ts:26 The closed vocabulary is checked at runtime by a type guard plus a fallback. There are no in-page hosts to compare against a declared list.
